Şirkət: AQA Şirkətlər Qrupu

Vakansiya: Data Scientist


Təsvir
Ferrum Capital, the first independent factoring company in Azerbaijan, is announcing a vacancy for a Python Developer.
 
Ferrum Capital LLC was established in 2017 as the first independent factoring company in the Republic of Azerbaijan and as a member of the AGA Group of companies, with the aim of providing factoring and other financial services to local and international companies.
The mission of Ferrum Capital LLC is to be one of the leading companies chosen by candidates who want to start their first work experience with us and achieve career growth while developing themselves.
 
We would like to inform you that a large part of the Ferrum Capital team consists of talented young professionals, and we are looking for new talents to increase their number. By joining our team, young professionals will have the opportunity to succeed and grow together with us


Tələblər
Required Technical Skills
The ideal candidate should be familiar with and have practical experience in the following areas:
Python programming language
Machine learning and deep learning algorithms and methodologies
Libraries and frameworks including Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, and Transformers
Design and development of question–answering systems and chatbots
Working with Large Language Models (LLMs), including fine-tuning and optimization
Implementation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques on LLMs
Development of applications based on RESTful architecture using Flask or FastAPI
Containerization and deployment of projects with Docker
Version control and project management using Git
Preparation of clear, well-structured, and practical technical documentation
Basic familiarity with MLflow and dashboard development tools (considered an advantage)

Additional information
 
·      5-day work schedule: 10:00 – 19:00

Şirkət: The International School of Azerbaijan

Vakansiya: Network and Systems Manager


The Network and Systems Manager is responsible for the design, maintenance, security, and reliability of the school’s technology infrastructure. This includes managing a custom multi-server environment, ensuring network uptime, overseeing cybersecurity practices, and providing high-level technical expertise to support teaching, learning, and administrative operations. The position job description can be accessed here 
Qualifications & Experience Needed

Required
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
Minimum 3–5 years of professional experience managing enterprise-level networks and servers. 
Demonstrated experience with backup and disaster recovery systems. 
Cybersecurity knowledge and experience implementing best practices. 
Ability to work in a fast-paced educational environment with excellent customer service skills. 

Strong expertise in:
Network design and troubleshooting. 
Windows and/or Linux server administration. 
Virtualization technologies.
Firewall administration. 
Active Directory and identity management 

Preferred
Experience working in schools or similar institutions. 
Certifications such as CCNA/CCNP, CompTIA Security+, Network+, Microsoft, or VMware. 
Experience with Google Workspace for Education. 
Familiarity with cloud migration strategies. 

Personal Attributes
Strong communicator who can explain technical concepts clearly. 
Collaborative team member who supports an inclusive and positive work culture. 
Calm under pressure with strong troubleshooting and analytical thinking abilities. 
Committed to reliability, security, and solving problems proactively. 
Respectful of confidentiality and data protection.

Interested qualified candidates are requested to fill in the Application Form and send to the e-mail address in the hr@tisa.az. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The instructor will conduct training sessions, develop lesson plans, deliver lectures, and guide students in understanding DevOps practices, tools, and technologies. Other responsibilities include mentoring students, evaluating their progress, and providing constructive feedback to ensure a hands-on and engaging learning experience.

Qualifications

Proven experience in Teaching, Training, or Lecturing in technical subjects
In-depth understanding of DevOps principles, tools, and processes
Strong communication and interpersonal skills for effective knowledge transfer
Ability to mentor students and adapt teaching methods to diverse learning styles
Familiarity with modern IT and software industry trends
Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or related fields is preferred

Requirements
Strong Linux fundamentals
Bash scripting (automation basics)
Git (advanced usage, branching strategies)
CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins and/or GitLab CI)
Docker (building and optimizing images)
Kubernetes (deployments, services, scaling, troubleshooting)
Terraform (Infrastructure as Code, modules, state management)
Configuration management with Ansible
AWS (EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, basic networking)
Monitoring and alerting (Nagios, Prometheus, or similar)
Basic security practices (secrets management, access control)

Application Prosess

Responsibilities
Triage Security Findings – Assess incoming bug bounty reports and scanner findings. Evaluate validity, calculate real severity, and escalate appropriately with clear written summaries.

Assist with Vulnerability Assessments – Participate in security assessments of web applications and APIs. Help identify and document risks in new features and existing systems.

Write Clear Security Documentation – Document findings, reproduce steps, and remediation guidance in a way that engineering teams can act on.

Support Threat Modeling – Participate in threat modeling sessions. Learn to identify trust boundaries, data flows, and attack surfaces in system designs.

Monitor Security Tools – Help operate SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning tooling. Track findings, reduce noise, and support remediation workflows.

Support Code Reviews – Review code for common vulnerability classes under guidance of senior specialists. Learn to identify security issues across PHP, Python, and Go codebases.

Stay Current – Follow developments in the security community. Bring awareness of new vulnerability classes, CVEs, and attack techniques relevant to our stack.

What You Bring
Web Security Fundamentals – Solid understanding of common vulnerability classes: OWASP Top 10, CSRF, XSS, IDOR, SQL injection, open redirect, authentication and session management weaknesses. You understand root causes, not just names.

Web and Browser Fundamentals – Solid understanding of how web applications work: HTTP request/response cycle, client-server model, REST APIs, how browsers handle same-origin policy, cookies and their attributes, and CORS. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

Security Testing Tools – Hands-on experience with Burp Suite or similar web application security testing tools. You have used them to intercept, modify, and replay requests - not just run automated scans.

Vulnerability Documentation – Able to reproduce a vulnerability and write it up clearly: reproduction steps, proof of concept, and impact statement. Findings that engineering teams cannot reproduce or understand do not get fixed.

Secure Development Awareness – Familiarity with foundational secure coding concepts: input validation, output encoding, parameterized queries, and least privilege.

Code Readability – Ability to read and follow code in at least one language relevant to web security - PHP, Python, JavaScript, or Go. You don't need to be a developer, but you need to follow logic and spot security-relevant patterns.

Analytical Thinking – You reason through problems methodically. You can explain not just what a vulnerability is but why it exists, how it is exploited, and what fixing it actually requires.

Clear Written Communication – You write findings and summaries that are precise, reproducible, and useful to the engineers who need to act on them.

Curiosity and Initiative – You dig into problems rather than stopping at the surface. When something looks wrong, you investigate before concluding.

Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and where security tooling fits
Exposure to cloud environments - GCP, AWS, or Azure
